variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
var x: i32 = 10;
let y: i32 = 20;
variables.notes: Variables use `var` for mutable and `let` for immutable (constants).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Carbon has explicit sizing for numeric types (e.g., i32, f32).

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
var z: i32 = x + y;
var b: bool = (x > y);

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals follow C++ syntax with parentheses.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Carbon syntax is still experimental; this reflects range-based iterations.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions use `fn` keyword with `->` for return types.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
// Experimental: map usage in Carbon is not fully stabilized.
// Typically relies on C++ interop or standard library structs.
maps.notes: Map syntax is experimental and subject to change.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Carbon aims to use sum types and optionals over traditional exceptions.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Carbon uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Carbon provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Carbon uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Carbon supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Carbon distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Carbon supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: Carbon evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: Carbon represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Carbon implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Carbon models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Carbon manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Carbon represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Carbon provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Carbon structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
